summary: A four-level model made visualization description scope and analytical content more explicit.
Research moved accessible visualization beyond alt text toward structured navigation and richer data access.
Empirical audits exposed widespread screen-reader barriers in real web visualizations.
Olli demonstrated an extensible structure-first accessible representation derived from visualization specifications.
Research made aggregation consistency failures in semantic layers and corrective rewrites explicit.
Chart Reader used co-design with screen-reader users to expand interactive accessible chart experiences.
Studies showed visual and numerical uncertainty representations can produce different decision patterns.
WCAG 2.2 added and consolidated testable accessibility obligations for modern interactive content.
SDMX 3.1 updated the editioned information/registry surface for statistical structures and exchange.
ODF/OpenFormula 1.4 refreshed open, editioned formula interchange semantics.
Provider semantic models increasingly expose metrics, entities, dimensions, joins and pre-aggregations as inspectable contracts.
Modern semantic runtimes increasingly separate semantic-query identity and roll-up containment from matching SQL text.
The research frontier increasingly evaluates task-equivalent nonvisual navigation rather than alt-text presence alone.
Current formula, visualization and accessibility standards preserve deterministic contract surfaces independent of optional generative assistance.
